cases.rationale: Tier-1 boxed warning match: a confirmed pregnant patient (first trimester, intrauterine pregnancy with cardiac activity) has near-daily exposure to two opioids (hydrocodone/acetaminophen and tramadol), creating risk of neonatal opioid withdrawal syndrome. The patient also nearly discontinued opioids abruptly, which carries maternal-fetal withdrawal risk. A taper plan is being coordinated but is not yet in place, so clinician review, monitoring, and follow-through are required.
cases.transcriptEscalation: Patient reported nearly flushing all opioid medications immediately after the positive pregnancy test ('I almost flushed everything down the toilet that night'). Although counseled in-visit, this impulse plus high baseline anxiety warrants close follow-up to ensure she adheres to the supervised taper and does not abruptly self-discontinue before the written taper schedule is in place.
cases.draftedAction: Review Ms. Melodee Satterfield's opioid exposure (Acetaminophen 300 MG / Hydrocodone Bitartrate 5 MG Oral Tablet; tramadol hydrochloride 50 MG Oral Tablet) during pregnancy. Counsel on neonatal opioid withdrawal risk, avoid abrupt discontinuation, and coordinate obstetric and pain-management follow-up with her pain specialist and Dr. Alvarez. Confirm the written gradual taper schedule is finalized this week, reassess pain control and taper progress at every prenatal visit, and plan neonatal monitoring for opioid withdrawal syndrome at delivery.

claims.text: The patient has a confirmed normal pregnancy documented as an active condition.
The patient is taking hydrocodone/acetaminophen 5 mg and tramadol 50 mg, confirmed as current during the visit.

citation.quote: the hydrocodone with acetaminophen — the five milligram tablets — and tramadol, fifty milligrams. Is that still current?

claims.text: Opioid use is near-daily, indicating sustained fetal exposure during pregnancy.

citation.quote: Hydrocodone for the bad days, tramadol for the medium ones. I don't take them every single day, but... most days is the honest answer, lately.

claims.text: The patient nearly discontinued opioids abruptly after learning of the pregnancy, a safety risk explicitly warned against.

citation.quote: I almost flushed everything down the toilet that night. Cody stopped me.

claims.text: The clinician counseled against abrupt discontinuation due to maternal and fetal withdrawal risk.

citation.quote: do not stop these medicines suddenly. Your body is used to them, and stopping cold turkey puts you into withdrawal — and withdrawal is genuinely risky in pregnancy, for you and for the baby.

claims.text: Neonatal opioid withdrawal risk was discussed and a coordinated gradual taper with the pain specialist was planned.

citation.quote: the baby can be born needing to withdraw, which is treatable but hard on everyone. So the plan is a careful, gradual taper, and I don't want you improvising it alone. I'll reach out to your pain specialist this week
